findings.title: M17.25: the nightly layered-500 reading varies between runner machines; median-of-3 in one job cannot fix it
findings.evidence: The 243 ms limit is perf-baseline.json layered-500 211 x 1.15 (NFR-PERF-005 regression budget, scripts/ci/perf-baseline.mjs:23), not LAYOUT_500_NODES_MS (2000); the row text says otherwise. Median-of-3 readings were 238 ms (2026-10-21) and 172 ms (2026-10-22) on the same code, 38 % apart across nights. The perf job runs on ubuntu-latest, while performance.md rule 20 requires a fixed runner.
findings.recommendation: Keep LAYOUT_500_NODES_MS, PERF_REGRESSION_TOLERANCE_PCT and the 211 baseline. Either (a) judge bench/calibration ratios from a frozen calibration workload run in the same job, with an ADR on how NFR-PERF-005 is judged and the acceptance changed (spec skill) to three consecutive nightlies' normalized readings within 15 %; or (b) a fixed or larger runner, which is a human decision. No retries, no dropping the bench, no picking non-consecutive nightlies. If neither fits in M17, set blockedReason and hand back.

findings.title: An upward perf-baseline.json re-record passes every gate
findings.evidence: check-drift does not read perf-baseline.json; perf-baseline.mjs hard-codes 1.15 instead of t('PERF_REGRESSION_TOLERANCE_PCT'); performance.md rules 18-19 name scripts/gates/perf-baseline.json and claim check-drift enforces them. M17.25 and M17.38 both touch this file.
findings.recommendation: Use the threshold; make check-drift refuse an upward baseline move without a Threshold-change: trailer, with a harness case; correct performance.md.

findings.title: M17.38 baselines from one hosted-runner reading would recreate the M17.25 flake at the 15 ms scale
findings.evidence: tree/radial/mindmap-500 baselines are 16/17/14 ms (local), so the 15 % budget is about 2 ms; 0ed7defa already judges them nightly, so the perf leg stays red until they are re-recorded; one nightly (39849966524) is planned as the source.
findings.recommendation: Make M17.38 depend on M17.25: record the three baselines in F1's units after it lands; until then use the in-flight nightly's numbers for information only.

findings.title: The FR-LAY-006 gate file judges 'moved <= 30 %' with the function under test
findings.evidence: incremental.test.ts:81 asserts metrics.moved === movedPercent(first, second) and then <= LIMIT; a mutant movedPercent returning 0 passes the whole suite (no unit case; no layout mutation floor). arrange.test.ts:126 has an independent oracle for tree only, with a literal 30.
findings.recommendation: Count centre moves > 0.5 px directly in the test for tree, force and packing; add a numeric unit case for movedPercent; read 30 from thresholds in arrange.test.ts.

findings.title: Plan asked for a T3 golden per template; only 3 of 9 are rendered
findings.evidence: Plan tasks 13-14 and gate leg 'T3 goldens pass'; templates.test.ts has T0 geometry goldens; examples/dsl/templates.flux.yaml renders only process.basic, matrix.2x2 and hierarchy.org; the m17 leg label says 'renders to its golden'.
findings.recommendation: Render all 9 templates (including process.chevron and venn's opacity) into normalized SVG goldens, for example by extending the templates example, and have the leg check every id.

findings.title: Two safe-area helpers
findings.evidence: packages/editor/src/layout-arrange.ts:199-221 re-implements SAFE_SHARE and safeAreaOf without the margin option or the clamp of the exported @fluxion/layout safeAreaOf (passes.ts:72), so Fit's notice can judge against a different area than the fit itself.
findings.recommendation: Use the exported safeAreaOf with the screen layout's margin.
